name: Lancers Cocktail Lounge
notes: Dive bar (est. 1963), cash-only. Official site (lancerscocktails.com) is address/hours/social links only, no menu of any kind. WebSearch on food items (wings/fries/burger) returned that the bar serves no food and patrons bring in food from across the street. No priced drink list found on the site, Facebook, or elsewhere. This is a drinks-only dive bar publishing no per-item prices anywhere -> not_found, not a capture limitation.

name: The Simple Coffee House
notes: No first-party ordering platform found (no Toast/Square/Clover). Priced from DoorDash's server-side schema.org Menu JSON-LD. Markup check: prices land cleanly on .00/.25/.50/.75/.95 with no consistent divisor pulling them to round numbers, so treated as face value, not a fee. Dropped the 'Most Ordered' section as a pure duplicate sample of items already in Coffee/Non Coffee/Food. Dropped 'Coffee Bean (Whole)' retail bagged-beans section as adjunct retail merchandise, not the drink/food menu. SinglePlatform (places.singleplatform.com) was also fetched and shows the same item names at 30-70% lower prices (e.g. Espresso $3.00 vs $5.00, Bagel $3.50 vs $6.00) -- per playbook this is SinglePlatform staleness, not evidence DoorDash carries a markup, so it was not used as a corroborating cross-check, just noted here. Sections: Coffee, Frappes, Non Coffee, Food -- plausible full shape for a small cafe.

name: Slowly Restaurant + Bar
notes: First-party WordPress/Divi site, address on page (1520 Garnet Avenue, San Diego, CA 92109) matches work list exactly. Three separate priced pages captured: dinner (slowlysd.com/main-course/), cocktails (slowlysd.com/cocktail-menu/), and Social Hour happy hour (slowlysd.com/social-hour/) -- all prefixed with their menu name since Social Hour and Truffle Fries ($8) genuinely differ in price from the dinner menu's Truffle Fries ($12). Dropped 'Oysters' and 'Branzino' from the dinner menu (both 'MP', no fixed price). Dropped 'Cocktails & Mocktails $5 Off' from Social Hour (a discount, not an absolute price). Also skipped the 'A Moment to Digestif' after-dinner spirits list on the cocktail page -- the HTML groups six spirit names (Amaro, Aperol, Campari, Fernet Branca, Jagermeister, Limoncello) under one detached '11' with a markup structure I could not confidently bind to each name, so left out rather than guess. Sections captured: Dinner (slow starters, Masterful Mains, Salads, Sides, desserts), Drinks (Signature Cocktails, Free Spirit zero-proof, Bloom, under the sun, Golden Slowdowns), Social Hour (food + drink specials). This is the full dinner + cocktail + happy hour menu as published; no lunch/brunch menu found on the site.

name: Nacho Taco Shop
notes: Widely listed elsewhere as 'Nacho's Taco Shop'; filed under the batch's exact name. No first-party site, and its UberEats store link (from WebSearch) 404'd to plain curl -- UberEats needs a browser/session, not fetchable here. No DoorDash storefront found either. Priced from menutoeat.com's schema.org Restaurant/hasMenu JSON-LD, which cites the business's own Google Maps place id (ChIJGfovvjp13IAR4yKzK-0YES8) as its source, so this reads as Google Business Profile menu data rather than a random scrape. Tried to find a second independent priced source to cross-check: zmenu.com and Yelp both 403'd (Cloudflare/bot wall), mymenuweb.com and goto-restaurants.com were empty JS shells with no prices in static HTML -- so this is a single-source capture, held at medium rather than high. Price-level check: a WebSearch summary independently reported this restaurant's per-person price as $10-20, consistent with the $9.80 carne asada burrito / $9.96 California burrito here; the $1.40-$3.65 individual tacos and $2.10-$4.20 plain-hamburger-and-fries items read low but are in line with typical San Diego County taco-shop pricing, not a stale outlier era. No markup pattern found (odd cents like .40/.80/.95/.30 don't divide cleanly by 1.04/1.10/1.15/1.20/1.25 onto round numbers -- looks like genuine POS pricing, not a fee). Sections captured: Breakfast Plates, Breakfast Burritos, Kids Meals, Hamburgers, Burritos, Tacos, Tortas, Nachos -- a plausible full taco-shop shape. No lunch/dinner plate section beyond these was found in the JSON-LD; if the shop has additional printed-menu sections (e.g. quesadillas, seafood -- the UberEats listing title says '& Seafood') they were not captured here.

name: Areli's Taco Shop
notes: Batch-listed website (arelistacoshop.site) is a dead domain -- DNS does not resolve at all, not just unreachable. No other first-party site found; res-menu.com mirror (arelis-taco-shop.res-menu.com) returned an empty 200. Priced from DoorDash. The page's server-rendered schema.org Menu JSON-LD only exposed 91 items across 11 categories (missing Burritos, Special Burritos, Breakfast Plates, Breakfast Burritos, Rolled Tacos, Drinks, Desserts entirely) -- per playbook this is the known DoorDash JSON-LD partial-catalog case, so the full 129-item / 17-category catalog was instead read out of the page's escaped Next.js RSC flight payload (MenuBookCategory list for category names/counts, MenuPageItem objects for name/description/displayPrice, matched to their real category via the category_id embedded in each item's logging block, not the 'Most Ordered' container they also appear under). Verified the extracted total (129) matches the sum of every category's numItems from the RSC payload, so this is the complete catalog, not another partial. Markup check: prices cluster on .99/.49/.75/.00/.50/.25 with no consistent divisor (1.04/1.10/1.15/1.20/1.25) pulling them onto round numbers -- ordinary POS pricing, not a delivery-platform fee. Sections: Breakfast Plates, Breakfast Burritos, Burritos, Special Burritos, Tacos, Mini Tacos, Rolled Tacos, Quesadillas, Tortas, Chimichangas, Nachos & Fries, Combination Plates, Soups, Tostadas, Seafood, Drinks, Desserts -- full shape for a taco shop, nothing held back as adjunct.
